claim: None justified: cross-task dynamics adaptation failures under matched one-step validation loss cannot be elevated to a general world-model vulnerability claim without breaking confounders with representation-geometry noise.
reasoning: The observed empirical results demonstrate overlapping confidence intervals across random, cascade, reverse, and shuffle interventions (walker returns spanning ~290 to ~398 without systematic ordering) while the target h3 branch dispersion remains essentially static (~2.09 to ~2.13) and one-step prediction errors remain invariant (~0.00085). The hypothesis that source-target action subspace alignment mediates downstream planning deterioration is empirically falsified by the provided data. Without an established downstream planning causal chain, any proposed geometric or spectral surrogate reduces to representation noise or standard negative transfer repackaged under alternative terminology. Under strict evaluation criteria, no candidate exceeds novelty 7.
falsifier: Demonstrating that the target policy return degradation in cascade order is statistically indistinguishable (p > 0.10 under a two-sided permutation test across 20 seeds) from arbitrary frozen-actor transfer under identical one-step dynamics loss.
